extracted.intended_audience: general readers and writers interested in simple living, self-reliance, and transcendentalist essays
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative statements for composing or exemplifying essays about simplicity, self-reliance, minimal clothing and shelter, and critique of fashion/civilization in a Transcendentalist prose voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object of clothing
rubrics_metrics.description: Let him who has work to do recollect that the object of clothing is, first, to retain the vital heat, and secondly, in this state of society, to cover nakedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clothing primarily for utility (warmth, modesty). Resist purchasing garments out of love of novelty or regard for others' opinions. Practicality should trump fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value durability and thrift in dress
rubrics_metrics.description: A man who has at length found something to do will not need to get a new suit to do it in; for him the old will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer durable, long-lasting garments (one thick garment rather than many thin ones). Cheap, sturdy clothes that last are preferable; one can buy simple durable clothing at modest prices so no one is too poor to be respected when clad in honest, self-earned garments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept patched clothes; improvidence is the vice
rubrics_metrics.description: No man ever stood the lower in my estimation for having a patch in his clothes; yet I am sure that there is greater anxiety ... to have fashionable, or at least clean and unpatched clothes, than to have a sound conscience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wearing patched or repaired clothes is not shameful; refusal to mend (improvidence) is the real vice. Test social expectations by accepting simple repairs rather than replacing garments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dressing for mere respectability or fashion
rubrics_metrics.description: He considers, not what is truly respectable, but what is respected. We know but few men, a great many coats and breeches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't let clothes define social rank; question whether outward respect mirrors inner worth. Resist following fashion authority ('They do not make them so now').

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward fashion authority
rubrics_metrics.description: When I ask for a garment of a particular form, my tailoress tells me gravely, 'They do not make them so now' ... as if she quoted an authority as impersonal as the Fates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not defer unquestioningly to impersonal 'they' about what is appropriate; insist on what you want and what serves your character rather than accept fashionable norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware enterprises that demand new clothes
rubrics_metrics.description: I say, beware of all enterprises that require new clothes, and not rather a new wearer of clothes. If there is not a new man, how can the new clothes be made to fit?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat proposals that prioritize appearance (new clothes) over inner change with suspicion. Prefer personal transformation to superficial upgrades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity as practicable bodily readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable that a man be clad so simply that he can lay his hands on himself in the dark, and that he live in all respects so compactly and preparedly, that, if an enemy take the town, he can ... walk out the gate empty-handed without anxiety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clothing and life should be compact, simple, and functional—so minimal that one remains self-sufficient and untroubled by sudden loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clothing as outer cuticle; moderation in outward accretions
rubrics_metrics.description: We don garment after garment, as if we grew like exogenous plants by addition without. Our outside and often thin and fanciful clothes are our epidermis ... our shirts are our liber or true bark, which cannot be removed without girdling and so destroying the man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize degrees of attachment to clothing: superficial outer layers are removable, but core coverings (metaphorical 'shirts') relate to identity. Avoid unnecessary accretions of dress that alienate from self.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of factory/clothing production motives
rubrics_metrics.description: I cannot believe that our factory system is the best mode by which men may get clothing. The condition of the operatives is becoming every day more like that of the English; and it cannot be wondered at, since ... the principal object is, not that mankind may be well and honestly clad, but, unquestionably, that corporations may be enriched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate modes of production ethically: prefer systems that clothe people honestly without exploiting labor. Aim high even if immediate profit fails—long-run aims shape outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal necessary shelter
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider first how slight a shelter is absolutely necessary. I have seen Penobscot Indians ... living in tents of thin cotton cloth, while the snow was nearly a foot deep around them ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question assumptions about how much house is needed; study examples of simple, sufficient shelters (tents, wigwams, pit dwellings). Prioritize function and sufficiency over superfluous comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economics of owning vs hiring shelter (cost measured in life)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of a thing is the amount of what I will call life which is required to be exchanged for it, immediately or in the long run. An average house ... will take from ten to fifteen years of the laborer’s life ... so that he must have spent more than half his life commonly before 'his' wigwam will be earned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess housing decisions by the human-life cost (labor/time) they require. Beware that owning expensive dwellings may consume life-energy and freedom; consider whether renting or simpler dwellings better preserve life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware houses that imprison rather than house
rubrics_metrics.description: They are such unwieldy property that we are often imprisoned rather than housed in them; ... I know one or two families ... have been wishing to sell their houses ... but have not been able to accomplish it, and only death will set them free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and acquire dwellings that preserve mobility and autonomy; consider movability as a virtue (Momus's critique that a house not movable is a defect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and restraint in furniture
rubrics_metrics.description: Why should not our furniture be as simple as the Arab’s or the Indian’s? At present our houses are cluttered and defiled with it, and a good housewife would sweep out the greater part into the dust hole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simple, necessary furniture. Remove unnecessary objects that distract from life and work; cultivate an interior economy where 'furniture of the mind' is attended to before material furnishings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line houses with beauty where they contact life
rubrics_metrics.description: Let our houses first be lined with beauty, where they come in contact with our lives, like the tenement of the shellfish, and not overlaid with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate beauty functionally and intimately with daily living rather than using ornament as superficial overlay. Prioritize meaningful aesthetic touches that directly enrich life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be mindful of social cost of luxury
rubrics_metrics.description: The luxury of one class is counterbalanced by the indigence of another. On the one side is the palace, on the other are the almshouse and 'silent poor.' ... The mason who finishes the cornice of the palace returns at night perchance to a hut not so good as a wigwam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or creating comforts, consider their social distribution and moral consequences. Avoid contributing to systems where visible luxury depends on others' deprivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live as a sojourner in nature; don't be tool of your tools
rubrics_metrics.description: The very simplicity and nakedness of man’s life in the primitive ages imply this advantage ... But lo! men have become the tools of their tools. ... We now no longer camp as for a night, but have settled down on earth and forgotten heaven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve a transient, purposeful relation to material possessions; design life so tools serve human aims rather than humans becoming servants of their tools and possessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prudence of provisional/temporary building methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Those in New Netherland ... dig a square pit in the ground ... floor this cellar with plank ... raise a roof of spars ... live dry and warm ... for two, three, and four years ... The wealthy ... commenced their first dwelling houses in this fashion for two reasons; firstly, in order not to waste time in building, and not to want food the next season; secondly, in order not to discourage poor laboring people ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When settling or starting out, prefer quick, economical shelters that meet immediate needs and avoid tying up resources that would better secure sustenance. Staged building can be prudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical ethics of borrowing and communal stake in enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: I borrowed an axe and went down to the woods ... It is difficult to begin without borrowing, but perhaps it is the most generous course thus to permit your fellow-men to have an interest in your enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow and reciprocate communal sharing of tools and resources; borrowing can foster generosity and shared investment in projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer meaningful aims over mere accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the long run men hit only what they aim at. Therefore, though they should fail immediately, they had better aim at something high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set high, principled aims rather than pursuing transient gains or accumulation; intentions shape eventual outcomes even if short-term failure occurs.
